snippets: The Executive tier costs exactly double the basic membership — $130 a year instead of $65 — and pays you back through a 2% annual reward, early shopping hours, monthly delivery credits, and extra savings on Costco’s service programs.

For anyone who finds the midday Costco crush physically draining — and that includes plenty of older shoppers, parents with small children, and anyone using a mobility aid — the early window is arguably worth as much as the 2% reward, because it converts the most chaotic store in American retail into a quiet neighborhood market. Practical notes: have your Executive membership card (physical or in the app) ready at the door, since entrance scanners verify tier; your Household Card holder shares the benefit; and pharmacy, optical, and food court hours may differ from the early floor hours, so call ahead if one of those is the reason for your trip.

Link your membership number to Costco Same-Day or Instacart even if you rarely deliver — a single hectic month where you use the $10 credit is free money. Shift your weekly trip into the 9 a.m. window at least once to see whether the calm hour changes how much you enjoy the chore; most converts never go back to midday. And if you carry the Costco Anywhere Visa, understand the stack: the card’s cash back and the Executive 2% are separate programs that both apply, so a big-box purchase can effectively earn both at once.

2% back on qualifying purchases (up to $1,250/yr) · Early 9 a.m. shopping hours · $10/month delivery credit · Extra discounts on Costco Services & Travel · Same shelf prices as everyone else · Strip away the marketing and the Executive tier is four benefits stacked on a regular membership. The anchor is the 2% annual reward: most of what you spend in the warehouse, on Costco.com, and through Costco Travel earns 2%, paid once a year as a reward certificate that arrives with your renewal notice and spends like cash at the warehouse — capped at $1,250, which would take $62,500 of annual spending to hit.
